body:
1. Incorrect issue title, you do refer to `[ngClass]`, not `NgStyle `

2. > Developers expect binding to be correct.

    To not have such surprises do not use `[ngClass]`

    see https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/13940#issuecomment-276079860

    and https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/13958#issuecomment-276245722

Perfect use-case for `[ngClass]` - is to generate dynamic class-name in runtime. When you don't know class in advance, for example `[ngClass]="getMyRandomClassName()"`. Or attaching multiple classes at once. Everything else could be solved within `[class.class-name]="true"` binding.

Related issues that i found quickly: 
- https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/15396
- https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/17274
- https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/5763
- https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/17092

rename.from: NgStyle removes existing style when applying array that contains with 2 empty slots
rename.to: NgClass removes existing style when applying array that contains with 2 empty slots

@tytskyi 
1. I updated the typo in the title. I will change to ngClass everywhere shortly, as this is not ngStyle.
2. Thanks for the workarounds. I should have listed it along with my bug report.

I looked at the 4 related issues you listed, and all but the top one is closed. Does that mean they are already fixed or won't fix? The top related issue mentions using both ngClass and class. I am only using ngClass in my repo. I think this is a separate issue.

Anyways, here is a precise case where it fails, and is clearly a bug. If you debug the code, you can see that it adds the class to both the add and remove list during the `ngDoCheck` call in ngClass.
